description: Required. The Participant this Demography record belongs to. Production builds it as uuid5("https://w3id.org/bdchm/Participant", <subject id> + ":<COHORT>").

Optional. The Visit (exam, form or record) whose table supplied the value. Production writes one Demography block per source table that carries sex, race or ethnicity, each linked to that table's visit, so one participant can have several Demography records. Leave empty for cohort-level tables with no visit.

Biological sex (SexEnum). Write the enum name (MALE, FEMALE, UNKNOWN), not the OMOP code. Older cohorts label this 'gender'; when the values are male/female it maps here. Single-sex cohorts set a constant (production: WHI writes FEMALE for every participant). Where sex is only implied by a skip instruction (FHS 'Male Participant (if male skip ...)' checkbox), production maps checked to MALE and everything else to FEMALE; use this only when the item was asked of every participant.
Example source variable description: Sex [Visit 7/NCS Derived Variable Dataset. DERIVE71]|Reported gender|Gender (F=Female, M=Male)|Medical History - Female Reproductive History: Male Participant (if male skip to Smoking Questionnaire/MD07)

description: A person who belongs to the sex that normally produces sperm. Meaning OMOP:8507. Write the enum name; production gold writes the OMOP meaning CURIE (OMOP:8507) in almost every block, a known production departure pending Anne's decision.

A person who belongs to the sex that normally produces ova. Meaning OMOP:8532. Write the enum name; production gold writes the OMOP meaning CURIE (OMOP:8532) in almost every block, a known production departure pending Anne's decision.

Not known, not observed, not recorded, or refused. Meaning OMOP:8552. Use for an explicit source code such as 'Unknown or other' (production: LTRC GENDER 'UNK'). Leave the slot empty when the value is simply missing. OMOP:8552 is a deprecated OMOP concept (invalid_reason D, non-standard); HM main still enumerates it as the UNKNOWN meaning, so it is kept.

Race (RaceEnum, multivalued). Write the enum name, not the OMOP code. Rules: (1) A Hispanic/Latino code inside a race or combined race/ethnicity variable sets ethnicity HISPANIC_OR_LATINO; production then writes race UNKNOWN for that code (MESA race1c=4, WHI RACE=4). (2) 'Other' or 'Some other race' has no BDC-HM value; production maps it to UNKNOWN. (3) More than one race: production writes the single value MORE_THAN_ONE_RACE when two or more race boxes are checked (FHS, WHI) or the source says multiracial; BDC-HM also allows listing each race, which is open (see questions). (4) Historical labels: 'Negro' and 'Colored' are BLACK_OR_AFRICAN_AMERICAN (the BDC-HM definition names 'Negro'); 'Caucasian' is WHITE; 'Chinese American', 'Oriental' and Asian subgroups (Asian Indian, Chinese, Filipino, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese) are ASIAN; Native Hawaiian, Guamanian or Chamorro, Samoan are NATIVE_HAWAIIAN_OR_OTHER_PACIFIC_ISLANDER. (5) A combined 'Asian/Pacific Islander' code cannot be split; production maps it to ASIAN. (6) 'Indian' alone is ambiguous (American Indian vs Asian Indian): check the codebook. (7) Single-race cohorts set a constant (production: JHS writes BLACK_OR_AFRICAN_AMERICAN). (8) A variable that records only one comparison (ARIC PULM21 RACE 'Whites'/'Otherwise') maps only the named category; leave the rest empty.
Example source variable description: Race [Visit 7/NCS Derived Variable Dataset. DERIVE71]|RACE|SPECIFY OTHER RACE|Racial or ethnic group|Race [Pulmonary Predicted Function, PULM21. Visit 2]

description: A person having more than one race. Meaning OMOP:45880900. Use for a 'More than one race', 'Multi-race' or 'Mixed' code, or (production rule) when two or more race boxes are checked.

description: Hispanic or Latino origin (EthnicityEnum). Write the enum name, not the OMOP code. Rules: (1) Any Hispanic subgroup answered yes (Mexican, Puerto Rican, Cuban, Dominican, other Hispanic) is HISPANIC_OR_LATINO. (2) A combined race/ethnicity variable: its Hispanic code is HISPANIC_OR_LATINO; codes worded 'not Hispanic' (e.g. 'White (not of Hispanic origin)', 'Black, not Hispanic') are NOT_HISPANIC_OR_LATINO; plain race codes ('WHITE') say nothing about ethnicity, leave empty. (3) Paired checkboxes (Hispanic / Not Hispanic) map each box. (4) A cohort recruited as entirely Hispanic/Latino sets a constant (production: HCHS/SOL writes HISPANIC_OR_LATINO). (5) A study-imputed default (FHS eth_sum 88 'Defaulted ethnicity') is not mapped by production.
Example source variable description: HISPANIC ORIGIN|Are you Spanish/Hispanic/Latino|MEXICAN, CHICANO, MEXICAN-AMERICAN|Racial or ethnic group|EXAM 1 RACE, TELEPHONE INTERVIEW|WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING BEST DESCRIBES YOU - ETHNICITY HISPANIC OR LATINO
